original_item.title: Verify Prover accepts IVC proofs from any user without censorship
original_item.summary: Censorship resistance ensured by self-hosting option. Service censorship is operational concern with user workaround.

reviewed_items.reasoning: This audit item concerns censorship resistance of an off-chain prover service. The counterexample scenarios (service censoring users, rate limiting) do not constitute security vulnerabilities in the smart contract protocol. The protocol architecture explicitly allows users to self-host prover services, making centralized service censorship a non-issue for security. The on-chain verification at Verifier.sol:275,326,348 provides the actual security guarantee - any valid proof will be accepted regardless of which prover generated it. This is an operational/availability concern, not a security issue.

counterexample_evaluation.assessment: The 03 stage counterexamples describe service DoS or censorship scenarios. These are plausible operational issues but NOT security vulnerabilities. The protocol is designed with the explicit assumption that users can bypass centralized provers by self-hosting. No on-chain state corruption or fund loss is possible from prover service unavailability.

guards_found.reason: IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof validates proof correctness regardless of prover identity
IWithdrawVerifier.verifyProof validates Groth16 proofs for single withdrawals

guard_analysis.bypass_method: N/A - Security is guaranteed by on-chain cryptographic verification, not by prover service

original_item.title: Verify queued jobs are persisted and not lost
original_item.summary: Job persistence is service quality concern. Lost jobs are recoverable via resubmission.

reviewed_items.reasoning: This audit item concerns job queue persistence in an off-chain prover service. Job loss in the off-chain queue has no security implications - users simply resubmit their proofs. There is no on-chain state associated with job queuing, and lost jobs cannot result in fund loss or protocol exploitation. The 03 stage correctly identified this as OUT_OF_SCOPE for on-chain security. This is a service quality/UX concern, not a security vulnerability.

counterexample_evaluation.assessment: The counterexample describes job loss in an off-chain queue. While this can occur in practice (service crashes, storage failures), it has no security impact. Users retain their IVC proofs locally and can resubmit to any prover service. No funds are at risk, no on-chain state is corrupted.

guards_found.reason: Proof generation is idempotent - same inputs always produce same valid proof. Job loss only delays proof availability.

guard_analysis.bypass_method: N/A - No security property to bypass

Off-chain: Job potentially lost due to service failure

CONCLUSION: No on-chain security impact from off-chain job loss

original_item.title: Verify processing jobs have timeout and recovery
original_item.summary: Processing timeout is service quality concern. No on-chain security impact.

reviewed_items.reasoning: This audit item concerns job processing timeouts in an off-chain prover service. Stuck or infinitely running jobs in the off-chain service have no on-chain security implications. The protocol does not depend on job completion within any timeframe - proofs remain valid indefinitely once generated. Users experiencing stuck jobs can cancel and resubmit to alternative prover services or self-host. This is purely an operational/SLA concern for service providers.

counterexample_evaluation.assessment: The counterexample describes jobs getting stuck in processing state without timeout. This is a real operational concern for service availability but has zero security impact. On-chain contracts have no awareness of or dependency on off-chain job state. No attack vector exists.

guards_found.reason: On-chain verification is stateless and has no timing dependencies on off-chain services

guard_analysis.bypass_method: N/A - No security property to bypass

Off-chain: No timeout mechanism (hypothetical issue)

original_item.title: Verify STATE-JOB-COMPLETED implies valid Groth16 proof available
original_item.summary: Completion state validity verified by on-chain proof submission. Off-chain audit ensures correct status reporting.

reviewed_items.reasoning: This audit item concerns the correctness of job completion status in an off-chain prover service. Even if the service incorrectly reports a job as completed without providing a valid Groth16 proof, this cannot compromise on-chain security. The on-chain verifiers (Verifier.sol:275,326,348) will reject any invalid proof. False completion status only affects UX (user thinks proof is ready, tries to submit, gets on-chain rejection). This is a service quality issue, not a security vulnerability.

counterexample_evaluation.assessment: The counterexample describes false job completion status. This could occur due to service bugs but has no security impact. The on-chain verification provides the authoritative check. Invalid proofs are rejected at the smart contract level regardless of off-chain status claims.

guards_found.reason: Rejects invalid proofs regardless of off-chain service claims

original_item.title: Verify STATE-JOB-FAILED provides error details for proof conversion failures
original_item.summary: Error reporting is UX concern. No security impact from missing error details.

reviewed_items.reasoning: This audit item concerns error reporting quality in an off-chain prover service when job conversion fails. Poor error messages or missing error details are purely UX issues with no security implications. A user who receives a generic error message faces debugging friction but no fund loss or protocol exploitation risk. The user can retry, try alternative prover services, or investigate their input proof. This is a service quality concern, not a security vulnerability.

counterexample_evaluation.assessment: The counterexample describes generic or missing error messages for failed jobs. This is a real UX issue but not a security concern. No on-chain state is affected by off-chain error reporting quality. Users can debug by trial and error or seek support.

guards_found.reason: Error reporting is informational only - has no effect on on-chain state or security

guard_analysis.bypass_method: N/A - No security property affected by error message quality
